program.title: BSc in Global China Studies
uncertain: total_required_credits is a calculated value: the PDF does not state a fixed total for the major; it is the sum of the required_credits of all groups (using the lower bound for credit ranges).

The program consists of a common core plus Track Study: students follow one of two tracks (Integrated Humanities and Social Science, Social Science). Within the Integrated Humanities and Social Science Track, students with CGA of 3.3 or above may apply for one of the Research Options (Applied Economics, Environment and Technology, Heritage and Cultural Sustainability, History, Language and Literature, Politics, Sociology). Summing all groups double-counts mutually exclusive tracks/options.
The 'HUMA/SOSC/SHSS Electives' group (24-27 credits depending on capstone choice) is recorded at the 24-credit minimum and has no specific course list in the PDF, so its courses array is empty.

Remarks in the PDF note that HUMA 1020, HUMA 1630, SOSC 1150, SOSC 1661, SOSC 3530 and SOSC 4290 were last offered in earlier years and subsequently deleted; they are kept in the lists as printed in the PDF.

The PDF header/footer shows '2026-27 GCS (4Y) (2025-26 intake)', i.e. the document is the 2025-26 intake curriculum rendered on a 2026-27 template; the year is recorded as 2025-26 per the intake year.

groups.name: Applied Economics Research Option Elective Course(s)
groups.note: Applied Economics Electives (3 courses, which should include two courses at 3000-level or above, from the specified elective list. Courses taken as Major Elective Courses may not be counted towards this elective requirement.) Any ECON courses are also allowed. Students in the Integrated Humanities and Social Science Track with CGA of 3.3 or above may apply for enrollment; they should take Honors Thesis or Honors Research with a primary focus in applied economics. Students who take an option MUST complete all requirements specified in addition to the major requirements.
